A write-ahead log is a mechanism that ensures database consistency in the event of a crash. It does this by requiring the database to write all changes to the log before they are written to the main database files. This ensures that, even if the database crashes before completing a write, the log will contain a record of all changes that were made. When the database is restarted, it can use the write-ahead log to recover all of the changes that were made before the crash.

When the database is restarted, it reads the write-ahead log to determine which transactions were in progress when the crash occurred. It then applies these transactions to the database, effectively replaying the changes that were made before the crash. This ensures that the database is restored to a consistent state, even if some transactions were not fully completed when the crash occurred.

The use of a write-ahead log allows the database to recover from a crash without having to recheck all transactions to determine which ones were committed or rolled back. This can be a time-consuming and resource-intensive process. Instead, the write-ahead log provides a concise and efficient record of all changes that were made, making it easier and faster to recover
